questions.prompt: What distinguishes acute from chronic stress in this lesson?
questions.answer: The time pattern of the demands or responses and opportunities for recovery, not a fixed diagnostic threshold.

questions.prompt: Does a stress response establish a diagnosis?
questions.answer: No; responses vary and symptoms may have other causes.
questions.feedback: State the limits of the timeline.

questions.prompt: Why distinguish a stressor from appraisal?
questions.answer: The circumstance and its interpretation are related but not identical; real demands still matter.
questions.feedback: Avoid implying that structural problems are imaginary.

questions.prompt: How should sudden serious physical symptoms be handled?
questions.answer: Do not assume they are stress; seek appropriate urgent medical care.
questions.feedback: Prioritise safety over a classroom technique.

scoring.knowledge: 1 point per correct answer; formative only. Use answer-specific feedback and delayed retest.
scoring.practice: Distinguishes time patterns, resources and recovery without diagnosis; identifies appropriate urgent and organisational responses.
scoring.transfer: Draw two fictional demand-response-recovery timelines. Identify a stressor, an observable response, a resource and a possible organisational change for each. Explain why duration is insufficient to judge severity.
scoring.pass: All four mapped course criteria require Level 2 evidence; no averaging away omissions or safety boundaries. Quiz score alone cannot certify competency.
